subject: DONE s388: exception-named `my` rename — B1 (eval capture) + B2 (later decl wins); branch merged, #291 unblocked
description:
CLOSED s388.  Branch `wip/s385-296` merged to main.  #291 is unblocked.

WHAT IT WAS.  Since the #290 direction-D flip, an EXCEPTION-partition name
(Pl::GlobalPartition — $a/$b plus the runtime-owned set) stayed `defvar` =
PROCLAIMED SPECIAL, so `(let (($a …)) …)` was a DYNAMIC rebinding: a closure
made inside lost the value at scope exit.  CL cannot lexically bind a
proclaimed special, so only a different SYMBOL fixes it.  Design ratified s386
(fable-answers-s385.md §1): option (a) RENAME; re-partitioning REJECTED
(~41ns/sort call, misses `my %ENV`, disturbs #287).

=== B1 — string-eval capture (s387, a062914) ===
In EVAL-MODE compilation the capture alist beats the special table
(fable-answers-s385.md §2a).  `_rename_free_eval_captures` rewrites a free
exception name the caller's alist carries to `$a__evalcap__N`; the thunk lists
the ORIGINAL name as the LOOKUP key.  The per-token rewrite was extracted as
the shared `_rename_use_token`.
PLUMBING the ruling did not name: eval-mode compiling runs in the
`pl2cl --server` SUBPROCESS, so capture names travel in a new `<captures>`
protocol header AND key `*p-eval-string-cache*` — without that, one eval string
used from two scopes reuses whichever emission compiled first (silent-wrong).
FILE-LEVEL CARVE-OUT: a file-level exception `my` in a file whose string eval
sits inside a NAMED SUB is left un-renamed (a named sub is hoisted out of the
file-level `let`; only promotion-to-cell reaches it, and that pass finds the
decl by its PERL name in the eval text).

=== B2 — a LATER declaration owns the uses after it (s388) ===
`_rename_decl_within` walked from its declarator to the end of the scope, so an
earlier `my $a`'s rename claimed uses belonging to a later `my $a`; the later
decl's own pass then found nothing left to rename (tokens already said
`$a__excl__0`) and its binding sat unread.  TWO spellings, both live, both
correct on main before the branch:
 - SIBLING, same scope — perl-tests/split.t declares `my ($a,$b) = split …`
   three times in one block; rows 294/302 read the FIRST split's values.
 - CONSTRUCT-scoped — found by PROBING the family, named by no failing row:
   `{ my $a = "O"; while (my $a = …) { print $a } }` printed the OUTER value.
`_ref_shadowed` sees neither: it inspects Block/Sub parents, and neither a
same-scope sibling statement nor a construct HEAD is a sibling of one.
FIX (in the rename walk, keyed on `_lexical_decl_scope` so the two agree by
construction — new `_redecl_region`):
 - same scope  → STOP at the LAST TOKEN OF THE STATEMENT.  perl does not
   introduce the new name until the statement finishes, so the redeclaration's
   own initializer still reads the EARLIER variable (probed:
   `my $a = "X"; my $a = "[$a]"` → `[X]`; `my ($a,$b)=(1,2); my ($a,$b)=($b,$a)`
   → `21`).
 - construct   → SKIP the construct, resuming after it, except the region
   `_lexical_decl_scope` names as evaluated OUTSIDE it (a `for my $x (LIST)`'s
   LIST, a condition-my's own statement).  Covers `for my $x`,
   `while (my $x = …)`, `for (my $x = 0; …)`.
 - nested block→ UNCHANGED, still `_ref_shadowed`'s call: positionally exact
   there (statements before the inner `my` are the outer variable's), which a
   whole-region skip would not be.

MEASURED s388: 19 probe rows over two probe files identical to perl; split.t
back to its 9 baseline fails; corpus-diff 2 of 111 files, both explained
(split.t = the fix; lc.t = a file-level `my $a` had been swallowing a later
`for my $a (0,1)` loop variable, now two variables again); gate 138 files /
5108 tests PASS; cache generation v2-137 → v2-138.
FULL SWEEP (the merge bar — Pl/t was green with both regressions live): GATE
clean, 0 new / 0 fixed / no LOST; TOTAL passing 18498 → 18508 (+10), all
newly-reachable rows in eval.t (+9, from B1) and my.t (+1), neither file's fail
set moved.

GUARD ROWS: Pl/t/transpile-test-10.t — 'string eval sees a renamed
exception-name lexical…' + 'a file lexical named $a reaches an eval inside a
named sub' (B1) and 'a later declaration of an exception name owns the uses
after it' (B2, 13 shapes in one row).  All test_transpile against perl.
